records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient#59
records.source: Performance depends on hardware, display size, theme, and concurrent work. The settings have predictable relative costs: detail is approximately quadratic, density is approximately linear, and blur is inexpensive for the six buffered themes. ``drift`` has no buffer, so its blur is a second wider pass per dot and is capped by :data:`DRIFT_HALO_MAX_PX`. The :data:`WORK_BUDGET` limits combinations of density and detail that would make the backdrop compete with analysis work. Hidden widgets stop rendering entirely.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.ResonanceEngine#1
records.source: A floor with particles on it, and the particles are sand on a vibrating plate. The physics is in :mod:`spacr.qt.resonance` and is worth one paragraph here because it is what makes this theme different from a particle system with a music-shaped wobble: a plate driven at one of its resonances has lines that do not move, sand is thrown off everywhere else and comes to rest along them, and the figure IS the nodal set. So there is a right answer for where a particle goes, and the drive decides which figure it is and how hard the sand is being shaken rather than deciding the motion directly.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.ResonanceEngine#3
records.source: WHY THE DRIVE IS READ IN :meth:`advance` AND NOT WHERE IT IS USED. Every other engine promises that a frame is a pure function of ``(seed, clock, size)``, and two tests hold it down: one shades the same clock on two threads and compares the bytes, another steps one engine twelve times and jumps a second straight to the same clock. Reading a real-time signal inside :meth:`shade` would break both, and it would break them on the SHADING THREAD, where the failure is a picture that differs from the one the GUI thread would have drawn. So the drive is an INPUT, set on the GUI thread between frames under the engine lock exactly as :meth:`set_palette` is, and the promise becomes "a pure function of ``(seed, clock, size, drive)``" -- which is the same promise while nothing is playing, and that is when the tests run.
records.context: Why the drive is read in :meth:`advance` and not WHERE it is used. Every other engine promises that a frame is a pure function of ``(seed, clock, size)``, and two tests hold it down: one shades the same clock on two independent execution paths and compares the bytes, another steps one engine twelve times and jumps a second straight to the same clock. Reading a real-time signal inside :meth:`shade` would break both, and it would break them on the shading independent execution path, where the failure is a picture that differs from the one the main GUI execution path would have drawn. So the drive is an INPUT, set on the main GUI execution path between frames under the engine lock exactly as :meth:`set_palette` is, and the promise becomes "a pure function of ``(seed, clock, size, drive)``" -- which is the same promise while nothing is playing, and that is when the tests run.

records.source: The setup screen shows one of these under its AI provider marks and one under its GitHub mark. records.context: The setup application view shows one of these under its AI provider marks and one under its GitHub mark. Pressing Install there runs the tool's own installer -- :func:`spacr.qt.ai.cli_install.run_install`, on a :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` background execution unit, never on the main GUI execution path -- and this panel shows what is happening: the command that is executing, the installer's latest line of output, a Cancel button, and at the end either the next step or a sentence the user can act on.
records.translation: सेटअप पेज अपने AI प्रदाता चिह्नों के नीचे इनमें से एक और अपने GitHub चिह्न के नीचे एक दिखाता है। वहाँ Install दबाने पर टूल का अपना इंस्टॉलर चलता है -- :func:`spacr.qt.ai.cli_install.run_install`, एक :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` वर्कर थ्रेड पर, कभी भी GUI थ्रेड पर नहीं -- और यह पैनल दिखाता है कि क्या हो रहा है: चल रहा कमांड, इंस्टॉलर के आउटपुट की नवीनतम पंक्ति, एक Cancel बटन, और अंत में या तो अगला चरण या एक ऐसा वाक्य जिस पर उपयोगकर्ता कार्रवाई कर सके।

records.source: A VIEW is one visit to one screen: it begins when the screen is shown (:meth:`begin_view`, from its ``showEvent``) and ends when it is hidden because the user went to another screen (:meth:`end_view`, from its ``hideEvent``). Minimising the window does not end it -- the owner passes only non-spontaneous events. Pins last for the view: returning to the screen with its live preview still open collapses the surroundings again, which is what a fresh arrival at that layout would get.
records.context: A view is one visit to one application view: it begins when the application view is shown (:meth:`begin_view`, from its ``showEvent``) and ends when it is hidden because the user went to another application view (:meth:`end_view`, from its ``hideEvent``). Minimising the window does not end it -- the owner passes only non-spontaneous events. Pins last for the view: returning to the application view with its live preview still open collapses the surroundings again, which is what a fresh arrival at that layout would get.

records.source: :data:`MODEL_5PL` fits :func:`five_parameter_logistic`, a 4PL with one more parameter that lets the curve approach its two plateaus at different rates. Real dose–responses are asymmetric — receptor occupancy with cooperativity, anything read through a saturating stain — and **a 4PL fitted to an asymmetric curve does not fail, it moves the EC50**: on the calibration series in ``tests/qt/test_dose_response_fits_an_asymmetric_curve.py`` a symmetric fit to a curve whose true EC50 is 1.0 reports 0.67, with a tight interval and an R² of 0.997.
records.context: :data:`MODEL_5PL` fits :func:`five_parameter_logistic`, a 4PL with one more parameter that lets the curve approach its two plateaus at different rates. Real dose–responses are asymmetric — receptor occupancy with cooperativity, anything read through a saturating stain — and **a 4PL fitted to an asymmetric curve does not fail, it moves the EC50**: on the calibration series in ``tests/qt/test_dose_response_fits_an_asymmetric_curve.py`` a symmetric fit to a curve whose true EC50 is 1.0 reports 0.67, with a tight interval and an R² of 0.997.
records.translation: :data:`MODEL_5PL` :func:`five_parameter_logistic` को फ़िट करता है, जो एक अतिरिक्त पैरामीटर वाला 4PL है, जिससे वक्र अपने दोनों पठारों तक अलग-अलग दरों से पहुँच सकता है। वास्तविक खुराक–प्रतिक्रियाएँ असममित होती हैं — सहकारिता के साथ रिसेप्टर अधिग्रहण, संतृप्त होने वाले स्टेन से पढ़ी गई कोई भी चीज़ — और **असममित वक्र पर फ़िट किया गया 4PL विफल नहीं होता, वह EC50 को खिसका देता है**: ``tests/qt/test_dose_response_fits_an_asymmetric_curve.py`` की कैलिब्रेशन शृंखला पर, जिस वक्र का वास्तविक EC50 1.0 है उस पर सममित फ़िट 0.67 रिपोर्ट करता है, एक संकरे अंतराल और R² 0.997 के साथ।

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#26
records.source: It is nonetheless **not the default**, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. The fifth parameter trades off against the Hill slope — many (slope, asymmetry) pairs draw nearly the same curve — so on the eight or ten concentrations a plate actually carries it is weakly identified, and the profile interval it produces is correspondingly wider. The module therefore offers it, fits it **from the 4PL solution** so the asymmetric search starts at the symmetric answer, and reports an extra-sum-of-squares F test of the one added parameter in :attr:`DoseResponseResult.asymmetry_p` so a reader can see whether the asymmetry was worth what it cost.
records.context: It is nonetheless **not the default**, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. The fifth parameter trades off against the Hill slope — many (slope, asymmetry) pairs draw nearly the same curve — so on the eight or ten concentrations a plate actually carries it is weakly identified, and the profile interval it produces is correspondingly wider. The module therefore offers it, fits it **from the 4PL solution** so the asymmetric search starts at the symmetric answer, and reports an extra-sum-of-squares F test of the one added parameter in :attr:`DoseResponseResult.asymmetry_p` so a reader can see whether the asymmetry was worth what it cost.
records.translation: फिर भी यह **डिफ़ॉल्ट नहीं** है, और यह एक निर्णय है, कोई चूक नहीं। पाँचवाँ पैरामीटर हिल ढलान के साथ अदला-बदली करता है — कई (ढलान, असममिति) जोड़े लगभग एक ही वक्र बनाते हैं — इसलिए एक प्लेट पर वास्तव में मौजूद आठ या दस सांद्रताओं पर इसकी पहचान कमज़ोर होती है, और इससे बनने वाला प्रोफ़ाइल अंतराल उसी अनुपात में चौड़ा होता है। इसलिए मॉड्यूल इसे प्रस्तुत करता है, इसे **4PL समाधान से** फ़िट करता है ताकि असममित खोज सममित उत्तर से शुरू हो, और जोड़े गए एक पैरामीटर का अतिरिक्त-वर्ग-योग F परीक्षण :attr:`DoseResponseResult.asymmetry_p` में रिपोर्ट करता है ताकि पाठक देख सके कि असममिति अपनी क़ीमत के लायक़ थी या नहीं।

records.source: spaCR had a fit-on-load, wheel-zoom, drag-pan image canvas already: the QC field browser's own ``_FieldView``. Item 473's raw-versus-enhanced window needed the same thing twice over, and a third copy of "a QGraphicsView with a pixmap in it" is how a codebase ends up with three that behave subtly differently. So the field browser's view moved here unchanged, under a name that says it is shared, and the browser goes on using it under its old one.
records.context: spaCR had a fit-on-load, wheel-zoom, drag-pan image canvas already: the QC microscope field of view browser's own ``_FieldView``. Item 473's raw-versus-enhanced window needed the same thing twice over, and a third copy of "a QGraphicsView with a pixmap in it" is how a codebase ends up with three that behave subtly differently. So the microscope field of view browser's view moved here unchanged, under a name that says it is shared, and the browser goes on using it under its old one.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.zoom_view#2
records.source: WHAT IS NEW HERE IS THE TIE. Two views of the same region are only worth putting side by side if they stay in register: a curator comparing a field with its enhanced self is looking for a difference between them, and a difference in where the two are pointing is the one difference that is not information. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` makes a group of views share one zoom and one scroll position, so zooming or panning any of them moves all of them.
records.context: What is new here is the tie. Two views of the same region are only worth putting side by side if they stay in register: a curator comparing a field with its enhanced self is looking for a difference between them, and a difference in where the two are pointing is the one difference that is not information. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` makes a group of views share one zoom and one scroll position, so zooming or panning any of them moves all of them.
records.translation: यहाँ जो नया है वह जुड़ाव है। एक ही क्षेत्र के दो व्यू को साथ-साथ रखना तभी सार्थक है जब वे संरेखित रहें: किसी फ़ील्ड की उसके संवर्धित रूप से तुलना करने वाला क्यूरेटर उनके बीच अंतर खोज रहा है, और दोनों कहाँ इंगित कर रहे हैं, इसमें अंतर ही वह एकमात्र अंतर है जो जानकारी नहीं है। :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` व्यू के एक समूह को एक ही ज़ूम और एक ही स्क्रॉल स्थिति साझा कराता है, इसलिए उनमें से किसी को भी ज़ूम या पैन करने पर सभी हिलते हैं।
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.zoom_view#3
records.source: The tie is on the VIEW and not on the window, because what has to match is the transform and the two scroll bars -- the things a view owns. Views in a group must show images of the same size for the tie to mean anything; the compare window builds both of its pictures from one region, so they do.
